speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify your symptoms: have you noticed any visible blood in your urine, and does the pain radiate to your groin? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis; REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Leukocyturia Present; Bacterial_Culture Negative; Cytospin_Stained_With_Hansel's_Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm. Urine_Culture: Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of binucleated eosinophilic cells in your urine strongly suggests eosinophiluria, which is a key marker for Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN). Did you notice a skin rash, oral ulcers, or joint pain alongside your fever and flank pain? Please also tell me if you have been taking any new medications recently, especially antibiotics like penicillins or sulfonamides.

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN). Given the eosinophiluria, negative urine culture, and symptoms persisting after antibiotic treatment for sinusitis, this is the most likely diagnosis. Please confirm if you developed a rash or joint pain shortly after starting your antibiotics.
